data.summary: The 10‑week plan balances new content with frequent practice, beginning with the weak Unit 9 topics and revisiting them later. Each week includes 5 focused study hours, concrete tasks, and a clear focus. The final two weeks are dedicated to mixed review and timed practice to build stamina for the AP Chemistry exam.

weeks.focus: Introduce thermodynamics fundamentals and review key concepts from Unit 9.
tasks: Read the textbook sections on entropy and absolute entropy (pages 312‑328).
Create a one‑page summary table comparing entropy changes for common processes.
Do 8 free‑response questions on entropy calculations; check answers with the scoring guide.
Watch a 20‑minute Khan Academy video on Gibbs free energy and write a brief explanation in your own words.
Complete a 10‑minute flashcard review of definitions (entropy, ΔS, ΔG).

weeks.focus: Deepen understanding of Gibbs free energy and begin electrochemistry basics.
tasks: Read the textbook chapter on Gibbs free energy (pages 329‑342).
Solve 6 FRQ style problems on ΔG and spontaneity; self‑grade.
Draw and label a galvanic cell diagram for a Zn/Cu cell.
Complete 5 practice calculations of cell potential using the Nernst equation.
Review flashcards for key equations (ΔG = ΔH – TΔS, E°cell).

weeks.focus: Cover foundational Unit 1 concepts to solidify atomic structure knowledge.
tasks: Read sections 1.1, 1.5, 1.7, 1.8 in the textbook.
Create a concept map linking moles, electron configuration, periodic trends, and ionic compounds.
Do 12 FRQ practice items on mole calculations and periodic trends; compare with answer key.
Watch a 15‑minute video on photoelectron spectroscopy and write 3 takeaway notes.
Quiz yourself with 20 flashcards on atomic symbols, valence electrons, and common ions.

weeks.focus: Explore chemical bonding and molecular geometry (Unit 2).
tasks: Read textbook chapters on bond types, Lewis structures, and VSEPR.
Draw Lewis diagrams for 10 different molecules, then predict shapes using VSEPR.
Complete 8 FRQ style questions on bond polarity and molecular geometry.
Watch a 12‑minute tutorial on resonance structures; create 3 resonance examples.
Review flashcards for bond types, formal charge rules, and hybridization.

weeks.focus: Introduce thermochemistry (Unit 6) and connect to earlier entropy work.
tasks: Read sections 6.1‑6.3 on endothermic/exothermic processes, energy diagrams, and heat transfer.
Sketch energy diagrams for 5 reactions and label ΔH and activation energy.
Solve 10 calorimetry problems involving heat capacity and specific heat.
Do 4 FRQ practice items that require interpreting enthalpy diagrams.
Create a one‑page summary linking entropy, ΔG, and enthalpy concepts.

weeks.focus: Study kinetics (Unit 5) and practice rate‑law problems.
tasks: Read textbook sections on reaction rates and rate laws.
Complete a table of reaction orders for 6 sample reactions.
Do 9 FRQ style questions on determining rate laws from data.
Watch a 10‑minute video on integrated rate laws; solve one example for each order.
Review flashcards for rate‑law symbols and common integrated equations.

weeks.focus: Cover equilibrium concepts (Unit 7) and begin acid‑base fundamentals (Unit 8).
tasks: Read sections on equilibrium introduction and equilibrium constants, plus acid‑base intro.
Calculate Kc for 5 equilibrium reactions and determine direction using Q.
Do 6 FRQ practice problems on equilibrium constant calculations.
Solve 5 pH/pOH problems for strong acids and bases.
Create a quick‑reference sheet for K, Q, pH, and pOH equations.

weeks.focus: Finish acid‑base equilibria, buffers, and revisit weak Unit 9 topics.
tasks: Read sections on weak acid/base equilibria and buffer systems.
Perform 8 buffer‑preparation calculations and determine pH.
Do 5 FRQ items on acid‑base reactions involving titrations.
Re‑solve 4 entropy problems from Week 1 to reinforce concepts.
Sketch a galvanic cell for a new redox pair and calculate E°cell.

weeks.focus: Mixed review of all units with emphasis on weaker areas (Unit 9, kinetics, equilibrium).
tasks: Take a 30‑minute timed mixed‑topic quiz covering the listed codes.
Review each incorrect answer using the scoring guide and rewrite the solution.
Do a set of 12 FRQ practice questions selected from past AP exams across these units.
Create a one‑page mind map linking entropy, Gibbs free energy, reaction rates, and equilibrium.
Flashcard rapid fire: 30 seconds per card for key formulas.

weeks.focus: Full‑length timed practice exam and final review.
tasks: Complete a 90‑minute full‑length AP Chemistry practice exam under timed conditions.
Score the exam using the official answer key; note topics with lowest scores.
Spend 30 minutes reviewing each missed question, focusing on underlying concepts.
Do a final 10‑question rapid review set covering all units.
Write a brief exam‑day strategy checklist (materials, timing, stress‑relief techniques).

data.final_week_advice: On exam day, trust your systematic problem‑solving process, manage your time by allocating roughly 1 minute per multiple‑choice question and 12‑15 minutes per free‑response. Stay calm, read each prompt carefully, and use your flashcard sheets for quick equation recall.
